title: Validate K-Guard MCP direction against public standards, reports, and competitor repositories
summary: Validated the K-Guard MCP product direction using public documentation, standards, reports, and public GitHub repositories only. No third-party website probing, crawling, fuzzing, brute forcing, exploit payloading, or active attack testing was performed. The validation supports K-Guard's opportunity: AI-generated code still fails security tests often enough to justify pre-deploy gates; OWASP access-control and exposed-metadata guidance aligns with bounded dynamic checks; MCP official documentation emphasizes authorization, consent, tool visibility, and local MCP risks; public MCP/agent scanners validate the market category; and Korean privacy guidance supports deeper Korean PII and composite identifier detection.

Broken access control, IDOR, force browsing, CORS mistakes, exposed .git metadata, and backup files are standard web risk categories.
MCP systems need authorization, consent, visible tool exposure, and local MCP execution controls.
MCP and agent security scanning is already a validated market category.
Korean unique identifiers and composite personal-data flows are a meaningful local differentiator.

title: Calibrate dynamic PII sensitivity for large-site HTML numeric noise
summary: Adjusted dynamic PII classification so HTML responses are treated differently from JSON/API responses. Large production-style HTML often contains build ids, account-state ids, product ids, and date-like numeric strings that can resemble invalid RRN, bank-account, or passport candidates. Dynamic HTML now only escalates strong identifiers when the signal is high-confidence/contextual, such as RRN_VALID, credit card, driver-license, CI/DI, or health-insurance field evidence. Invalid RRN candidates, generic bank-account-looking numbers, and passport-like product ids in HTML no longer trigger DYN_RESPONSE_PII_LEAK. JSON/API responses remain stricter: bank-account JSON and bulk user JSON still trigger high findings. Added local black-box site-scale calibration script and report covering large general HTML noise, medium public contact page, small vibe-coded bulk JSON, valid strong identifier HTML, and bank-account JSON.
safety_boundary: No unauthorized external websites were actively probed during this calibration.

This reduces large-site false positives while preserving high findings for valid RRN, bulk JSON personal data, and bank-account JSON.

title: Add 10k-ready passive homepage calibration runner with checkpoint and resume
summary: Expanded passive_homepage_calibration.py from a small one-shot public homepage calibration script into a 10k-ready manifest runner. It only sends GET / requests, never OPTIONS, /admin, /api, .env, .git, backup/debug paths, or recursive crawling. Added --max-targets for sharding, --delay-ms for rate limiting, --checkpoint-jsonl for per-target raw-free crash recovery, --resume for continuation, --timeout, and --max-body-bytes. Added documentation for 10k-scale passive homepage calibration. A 10-target passive homepage sample was run before this entry and showed that strong identifier false positives on large/medium general homepages dropped to 0 after HTML JWT/Luhn noise calibration. The 10k arbitrary public crawl itself was not executed in this environment; the runner is ready for a user-supplied/approved manifest or an offline/public-crawl-derived target list.

Generated datasets/tranco-passive-homepage-10k.csv with 10,000 rows. Passive homepage calibration now separates redirect boundary observations from actionable high/critical findings, so common large-site redirects to www or other hostnames do not inflate vulnerability rates. Debug/error detection was tightened so normal HTML/JS strings such as TypeError labels are not treated as exposed stack traces unless stack-frame context exists. A live passive GET / smoke run over the first 100 Tranco targets passed with actionable high/critical target rate 0.0 and strong identifier target rate 0.0; redirect boundary observations are retained as a separate boundary_target_rate.

The first run surfaced one DYN_RESPONSE_PII_LEAK caused by DRIVER_LICENSE=1 on an English legal/benefits page; raw-free review showed this was likely license-context noise. Tightened Korean driver-license detection so 'license' alone no longer counts as 운전면허 context, while driver, driver_license, 운전면허, 면허번호, and CSV driver_license fields remain detected. title: Fix contest-grade benchmark and supply-chain scope before CTO review
summary: While validating whether K-Guard is strong enough for a real open-source developer competition, the strict benchmark exposed two release-readiness issues. First, direct script execution had used a stale editable install until the checkout was reinstalled; after reinstall, collector exclusions were expanded so ignored local scratch directories such as tmp/, terminals/, and test caches are not scanned as product input. This restored benchmark all_met=true with self_repository down to 100 files and 3.111MB. Second, dependency audit, SBOM, and license gates were scoped to declared project dependencies and extras rather than the whole developer workstation, removing unrelated global-package noise while keeping the dependency gate strict for runtime/dev/mcp declarations.

contest_readiness_guardrail: This evidence supports finalist or prize-contender technical readiness under a security/devtool category, but not a guaranteed grand-prize outcome.
Performance passes the current benchmark but has thin headroom on synthetic throughput, so a grand-prize bar should treat performance optimization and packaging polish as remaining risks.
Do not claim broad real-site vulnerability coverage; real-site evidence is a 10-site passive homepage smoke only.
External CTO review quorum is still required before claiming 대상급 readiness.

title: Promote K-Guard to a five-gate signed release-control engineering scope
summary: Implemented the requested hardening across static breadth, ecosystem execution, runtime mediation, agent identity, database access, and empirical validation. Guardian high now requires deep multilang, software composition, Streamable HTTP runtime, agent/database controls, and field accuracy. Added a pinned 9-language 90-case Semgrep pack, real Python/npm/Go SCA with bounded parsers, default-deny JIT/JEA grants and HMAC audit, SQLGlot AST/RBAC/EXPLAIN/SQLite isolation, exact target staging, hashed dependency closure, fail-closed suppression attestation, reproducible archives, fresh-wheel execution, and GitHub OIDC/Sigstore SLSA plus CycloneDX SBOM attestations. Product release remains deliberately held because the owned/partner field roster is empty.
